slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Azure is pay as you go, which sounds reassuring until the first bill arrives that nobody can explain. It is almost never one big mistake. It is a dozen small ones nobody owned.

slots.label: List item 1
slots.default: Virtual machines sized for a worst case that never arrives

slots.label: List item 2
slots.default: Dev and test environments running outside working hours

slots.label: List item 3
slots.default: Orphaned disks, snapshots and public IP addresses

slots.label: List item 4
slots.default: Pay as you go rates on permanently running workloads

slots.label: List item 5
slots.default: No tagging, so no accountability for spend

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Virtual machines get sized generously during a project and never revisited, so you pay for headroom you have never touched. Test environments spin up on a Tuesday and run all weekend because switching them off was somebody’s job in principle.

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Disks and public IP addresses outlive the machines they belonged to and keep billing quietly on their own. Nothing is tagged, so when the bill goes up nobody can say which project or department caused it.

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: Running everything at pay as you go rates when the workload is clearly permanent is the most common overspend we find. Reservations and savings plans exist precisely for predictable workloads, and applying them properly is often the single biggest reduction available without changing a thing technically.

slots.label: Paragraph 6
slots.default: None of this needs heroics. It needs somebody looking every month, which is what management means in practice rather than in a brochure.
